gap: Measure and gutters: A sets ~160 characters per line (2880px of text at an 18px advance) with literally 0px padding — the '#' of the H1 starts at x=0 and the last 't' of 'about that' terminates at x=2879, glyphs kissing both window frames — while B holds ~66ch inside a 1600px column with ~640px of left gutter. Compounding it: line pitch 42px on ~30px type = 1.40 leading vs B's 72px on 40px = 1.80; and A is 100% monochrome — zero coloured pixels anywhere in the body — so '#', '##', '-', '*' and '**' render at the identical pure #FFFFFF as the prose, with no bold, no italic, and no caret at the insertion point.
gapTheirs: Vertical economy: at 72px pitch and ~40px glyphs (≈20px CSS), B fits only ~13 body lines in 1800px and pushes the bulleted list and the closing 'She untied the skiff...' line below the fold entirely, where A shows the whole piece end to end. B also keeps the literal '**' and '*' in the text flow at full monospace advance (greyed to ~#7B7B7B), so '**bottle**' still eats four cells and shunts the line.
verdict: A is a raw textarea with the padding property forgotten: prose running the full 2880px edge-to-edge at 160 characters a line, so your eye loses the return sweep on every wrap, and 1.40 leading that jams descenders into the next line's ascenders. Worse, nothing is typeset — the '#' is the same pure white as the sentence it heads, '*Nothing out there is ever in a hurry,*' stays upright with visible asterisks, and there is no caret at all, so you cannot see where you are typing. B is the only one of the two that has been read by someone: 66ch measure, 1.80 leading, near-black #1C ink on #F9F9F9, true bold and true italic, markers demoted to grey, and a 6px #00B5FF caret sitting the full line box. B costs you the bottom third of the passage; A costs you the ability to read a sentence twice.

states.name: quattro
states.gap: Measure: A sets 169 characters per line across a 2774px full-bleed column (left inset 1px — the H1's '#' is literally shaved by the viewport edge, top padding 10px), versus B's 71-char, 1514px column centred in ~675px gutters. On top of that A renders zero typographic hierarchy: H1 cap-height 22px with 3px stems is pixel-identical to body cap-height 22px with 3px stems, same #FFFFFF, and '*Nothing…*' / '**bottle**' stay upright regular — no italic, no bold, markers the same white as the prose. A also contains not one saturated pixel: no caret is drawn at all.
states.gapTheirs: Vertical economy: 72px leading on a 30px cap (~1.7em) with blank lines taking a full 144px means only ~13 body lines fit 1800px — the closing paragraph 'She untied the skiff…' is pushed off-screen entirely, where A shows all 12 lines of the piece. The 3px × 36px #00B5FF caret is also the single saturated element on an otherwise #1C1C1C/#9E9E9E/#F9F9F9 neutral page, a hot cyan bar out of key with everything around it.
states.verdict: A is not typeset, it is dumped: 169-character lines running edge to edge, the heading hash clipped in half at x=0, five CSS px of air above the title, and pure #FFFFFF glaring off #2D2D2D so the counters bloom. Every markup character in A wears the same white as the prose and the headings are the same size and the same 3px stem as the body, so the document has no shape at all — and there is no caret, so you cannot see where you are typing. B's leading is on the loose side and it wastes a screen's worth of height (last paragraph gone), and that cyan caret is louder than anything else on the page, but it is the only one of the two where the eye returns cleanly to the next line and where bold reads as bold. Nobody writes a second draft in A.

states.name: mono
states.gap: Measure and margin: A sets ~155 characters per line (18.1 device px advance across a 2860px ink span) full-bleed from x=2 CSS px to x=1430 CSS px — literally zero margin, the '#' touching the window frame — against B's 62ch column with 336/338 CSS px gutters. Compounding it, A is 15px type on a 21px line box (line-height 1.40, only 15 device px of air between one line's descender and the next line's cap) vs B's 20px on 36px (1.80, 41 device px of air).
states.gapTheirs: Marker ink is too weak to edit against: B's '#', '##', '**' and '*' render at #9E9E9E on #F9F9F9 — 2.5:1 contrast, under the 3:1 floor — while the body sits at #1C1C1C, 16:1. Worse, the ghost markers still occupy full monospace cells, so '**bottle**' shows as true bold flanked by four faint smudges of dead grid. A prints every mark at #FFFFFF/13.7:1 where you can see whether you typed one asterisk or two.
states.verdict: A is a text file dumped into a window: 155-character lines running edge to edge with a 2px margin, and by the third line your eye can no longer find the start of the next one. It has no typography at all — '# The Lighthouse', '**bottle**' and '*Nothing out there…*' are rendered in the exact same 15px regular weight and the exact same #FFFFFF as the body, so a three-level document reads as one undifferentiated slab, and the caret is a 1px white hairline parked at 0,0 clipping the hash. B is 62ch, 20px/1.80, real bold, a real italic cut, and a 3px #00B5FF caret at the insertion point; its sins are that the headings get no size step (H1, H2 and body all sit at 29–30 device px cap height, weight-only hierarchy) and its markers are nearly invisible. Faint markers are an argument; 155-character lines are not.
